clue.text: Ability of planners to get piece on board vessel

parts.note: a draughtsman is a piece used on the board in the game of draughts (checkers)
a ship is a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a game piece aboard a boat, while planners show off their skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece on board' is not a plank on a deck but a counter in draughts, the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Draftsmanship is the skill of drawing plans, the ability architects and planners need.

clue.text: One can't sink any lower than this

definitions.text: One can't sink any lower than this

parts.words: One can't sink any lower than this
parts.note: two senses at once: this salt lake is the lowest place on land, and its salty water keeps a bather afloat so nobody can sink in it

explanation.surface: A despairing remark about having hit rock bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The lake between Israel and Jordan lies at the lowest land elevation on Earth, and its brine stops swimmers going under.

clue.text: Move swiftly along a river bank

parts.note: a bank is a row, as in a bank of seats

explanation.surface: Travel quickly beside a stream's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to dart or shoot straight like a missile from a bow.

clue.text: Sticky stuff ruined fridge? Heavens above!

parts.note: goo is any sticky substance

indicators.note: a ruined fridge is wrecked, so its letters are broken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds their refrigerator wrecked by gunk and exclaims in dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or dismay.

clue.text: Wartime leader has to accept it

indicators.note: the word to takes in the word it, holding it inside

explanation.surface: A general is forced to put up with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Josip Broz Tito led the Yugoslav partisans in the Second World War before ruling Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Can the most powerful man get the pick of the dancing-girls?

parts.note: may is used for can, as in 'may I go?'
on a chessboard the queen is the strongest piece, or 'man'

explanation.surface: Is the mightiest male allowed to choose a dancer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' sounds like a male ruler, but chess pieces are called men and the strongest is female.
explanation.definitionFit: On the British spring festival of May Day, a girl is chosen as the festive queen to lead the dances round the maypole.

clue.text: Given a choice, pick out a bit of Mexican food

indicators.note: we are told to pick a run of letters out of the words given

explanation.surface: Offered options, choose a Mexican snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip topped with cheese is a classic Tex-Mex snack.

clue.text: Fellow-composer pinching notes of a Mendelssohn overture?

parts.note: he stands for a fellow or male

indicators.note: the composer's name steals and holds two notes inside

parts.note: Havergal Brian was an English composer
D and E are notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A fellow composer is accused of stealing tunes from Mendelssohn.
explanation.walkthrough: Mendelssohn's 'Hebrides' overture (Fingal's Cave) depicts the Scottish islands; the adjective names it.
explanation.definitionFit: The overture is named after the Scottish island chain, so the adjective from those islands describes it.

clue.text: Soft in the brain, such a person?

parts.note: p (piano) means soft in music
the head houses the brain

explanation.surface: Is a simpleton someone soft in the head?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: a fool is 'soft in the head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is a stupid person, someone soft in the head.

clue.text: Publicise big shot suitable for taking off

parts.note: to air an opinion is to make it public
a worthy is an important, notable person

explanation.surface: Advertising an important figure, said to be fit to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft judged fit for flight is certified safe to take off.

clue.text: Simple accommodation for the middle class, in the main

definitions.text: Simple accommodation for the middle class, in the main

parts.words: Simple accommodation for the middle class, in the main
parts.note: reads like basic lodgings for the bourgeoisie generally, but 'the main' is the sea: on an ocean liner the intermediate fare grade between first and tourist was named after this kind of room

explanation.surface: Modest housing provided for middle-income people, by and large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' seems to mean 'mostly'; it is the old word for the open sea, putting us on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hut, or a sleeping room on a ship, is a basic place to stay.

clue.text: E.g. waste — tons of it removed for treatment

indicators.note: the letter for tons is said to be taken away from the jumbled pool of letters
letters sent for treatment are processed and come out in a new order

parts.note: the abbreviation for 'for example' supplies its two letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rubbish, for instance, with a great many tons of it being taken off to be processed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix EGWASTE with T taken out ('removed'); 'for treatment' signals the rearranging of what is left into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is the liquid refuse carried away by drains, a kind of waste matter.

clue.text: Wear diamonds kept in reserve

parts.note: to put on clothes is to wear them
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone sports jewellery that is normally locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan shelved for later is postponed, held back for future use.

clue.text: Foreign worker mostly paid in gold — rand

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: most of the word for paid is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: paid is taken as it is before trimming
R is the abbreviation for the rand, South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: An overseas labourer is paid largely in gold and in South African money.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young person from abroad living with a family and doing childcare and housework in exchange for board.

clue.text: Go through aboard one banger

parts.note: go is energy or vigour, as is pep
per means by way of or through
on means on board
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Pass through on a single noisy firework.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage, not a firework or old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy Italian-style salami is a kind of sausage.

clue.text: Knowing about books English novelists haven't finished

indicators.note: each novelist's name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: H. G. Wells, author of The Time Machine, was an English novelist
Charles Reade, author of The Cloister and the Hearth, was a Victorian English novelist

explanation.surface: Bookish knowledge, with English writers who never completed their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haven't finished' docks the last letter from both writers: WELL(S) and READ(E).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has read widely is learned and knowledgeable about literature.

clue.text: Fire, enthusiastically involved with attack

parts.note: to light is to set fire to
to be into a hobby is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: An eager arsonist goes on the offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone, verbally or physically, is to assault them.

clue.text: Scholastic life a person working on books intended to take up.

parts.note: a CA (chartered accountant) keeps the accounts, or books

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: aimed means intended

explanation.surface: Life in college as a bookkeeper meaning to start a career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To take up' turns AIMED into DEMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: A set of characters, kind and brave

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
to face something is to brave it, confronting it boldly

explanation.surface: A group of people described as generous and courageous.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is a single design of printing letters, a font.

clue.text: Trade in a lot of vehicles

definitions.meaning: to deal in goods, usually illicitly
the cars and lorries on the roads

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to deal illegally, and the noun means vehicles moving on roads.

clue.text: Unloading left, right, and centre in this country

indicators.note: the leftmost and rightmost letters of Unloading are taken

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the single middle letter of the nine-letter word Unloading

explanation.surface: Cargo being discharged everywhere in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left, right, and centre' looks like an idiom for 'everywhere'; instead take U and G from the ends of Unloading, add AND as written, then A from its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is an East African nation, so it fits as a country.

clue.text: A little short, getting by, or very, poor

indicators.note: the first piece gets, or receives, the next one inside it
the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: small means little

explanation.surface: Slightly lacking money, managing to survive, or desperately poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of the synonym for little, and 'getting' means the A-plus-trimmed-word pair receives the word by inside, just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means dreadful, extremely bad.

clue.text: Beginning of many calls, as a novelist welcomes company

indicators.note: a host who welcomes a guest takes them inside, so the novelist's name holds the next piece

parts.note: Charles Reade was a Victorian English novelist

explanation.surface: A writer receives visitors, as phones ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialling prefix digits begin many phone numbers, identifying the region being rung.

clue.text: Line removed from theatrical part for enchanting female

indicators.note: the line is taken out of the theatre area

parts.note: the circle is a seating area in a theatre

explanation.surface: A line cut from an actor's role for a charming woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatrical part' looks like a role, but is a section of the auditorium.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey this sorceress turns men into pigs, an enchantress.

clue.text: Dull and conventional close

definitions.meaning: of a room or weather: airless and muggy

explanation.definitionFit: Stuffy means both prim and old-fashioned and lacking fresh air.

clue.text: Escaped from wild animal up North

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom

parts.note: a wolf is a wild animal

explanation.surface: Someone fled from a wolf in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Having fled, a bird that has gone has taken off and got away.

clue.text: One member of family in the academic stream?

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: Is a relative at university?
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames is called the Isis where it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford stretch of the Thames bears this name, a river through a university city.

clue.text: The best part, they say, of the meal

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: the flower of something is its finest part, as in 'the flower of youth'

explanation.surface: A remark that something is the choicest portion of a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal' looks like a dinner, but here it is ground grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Flour is finely ground grain, and meal is a coarser powder of the same kind.

clue.text: Steer badly and commit offence within motorway system

indicators.note: the wrongdoing sits inside the motorway-and-system pair

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written M and the figure one, read as MI
a form is a set method or system
to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: Driving poorly and breaking the law on a road network.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords read its figure one as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdirect or give false information is to lead someone the wrong way.

clue.text: In which malice in person's exploded?

definitions.text: In which malice in person's exploded?

indicators.note: the letters are blown apart and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
here the S of the possessive counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A description of a killing where someone's spite boiled over.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of MALICEINPERSONS is used, and the clue as a whole also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime of passion is one committed in a fit of rage or jealousy, exactly when spite boils over.
